sn9.11:1.1: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.11:1.3: he kept on thinking evil unwholesome thoughts, that is, thoughts of sensuality, ill will, and harming.
sn9.11:1.4: Then the devatā that inhabited that woodland thicket, having compassion for that bhikkhu, desiring his good, desiring to stir up a sense of urgency in him, approached him
sn9.11:2.2: You, sir, are eaten by your thoughts.
sn9.11:3.1: “By basing your thoughts on the Teacher,
sn9.11:3.2: On Dhamma, Saṅgha, and your own virtues,
sn9.11:3.3: You will surely attain to gladness,
sn9.11:3.4: And rapture and happiness as well.
sn9.11:3.5: Then when you are suffused with gladness,
sn9.11:3.6: You’ll make an end to suffering.”
sn9.11:4.1: Then that bhikkhu, stirred up by that devatā, acquired a sense of urgency.
